newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef trading was steady to firm on mostly moderate demand and offerings, USDA said.

Retail demand was rather slow this week, both for immediate and forward interest. Most Choice cuts showed some firmness early in the week, especially the loin cuts, while the Select cuts were steady at best.

The Choice rib cuts traded higher at the start of the week, but as the week progressed , these cuts lost their early week gains and traded steady at week's end. The chuck and round cuts started higher and ended the trading period on a weak undertone on both the Choice and Select grades.

Closely trimmed items were steady to firm with loin cuts showing the most advances. Beef trimming were lower on light to moderate demand and moderate to heavy offerings. Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were steady to lower with the most downward pressure on the fed cattle grinds on light to moderate demand.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal generally steady; Select and Choice chuck primal steady to 1.00 higher; Select and Choice round primal steady to 1.00 higher; Select and Choice loin primal 2.00 to 3.00 higher; Closely trimmed items .50 to 1.00 higher; Beef trimmings 6.00 lower; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items steady to 3.00 lower.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up .91 at 107.38; 700/850 Up .84 at 107.07; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up .38 at 101.49; 700/850 Up .31 at 100.86.

COW and BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT While the slaughter cow receipts were moderate in most areas, the total cattle slaughter was higher throughout the week. As a result, supplies of alternative grinding material continued to be heavy.

Demand for fast food grinding needs was light because of backed up inventories of finished product, which caused boneless beef to lose last week's price gains. As demand declined, cow slaughter numbers were cut back late in the week and live prices weakened. The cow carcass market, however, managed to hold steady. The cow cuts market continued to experience light to moderate demand and offerings.

The 100% lean items traded generally steady as a slight decrease in demand, coupled with increased offerings, caused price spreads to narrow. Utility carcasses steady; Cutter firm compared to last market test; 90% boneless beef 4.00-7.50 lower; 85% 7.00 lower; 75% weak early; 65% 3.50-4.00 lower.
The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, May 08, 1997 was estimated at 78.08 per cwt., down 3.17 from a week ago Friday.
